1episcopus: short i (Lewis & Short ĕpīscŏpus, taking the heavy syllable for a long vowel). Greek ἐπίσκοπος, from ἐπί, with short ι, and σκοπός. Lewis & Short leave the i unmarked in their own compounds chōrĕpiscŏpus, cŏĕpiscŏpus and pseudŏĕpiscŏpus.

episcopus1, episcopī m.

noun, second declension

Greek ἐπίσκοπος, an overseer; Cicero once calls himself one, in Greek (Att. 7.11, Lewis & Short). The same word in East and West.

Other words

  • antistes, antistitis m. — a bishop; classically a high priest

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Cod. Just. 1.3 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. bishop

    Classically the overseer of a temple, a high priest (Cic., Liv.); the Christian writers use it of a bishop.

Examples

  • 2Mediōlānium: long o (the loci collection’s Mediolānium). Lewis & Short Mĕdĭōlānum.

    et vēnī Mediōlānium ad Ambrosium episcopum2

    and I came to Milan, to Ambrose the bishopAug. Conf. 5.13.23

See also priest, deacon, cathedral, church.
